focus: Validated fixed-name and dynamic AJAX handlers against their real nonce and capability paths.
Checked shortcode renderers and stored-option/user-meta sinks raised by Phase 1 and Semgrep.
Prioritized file writes/deletes, option updates, exports, and remote-request paths for low-privilege impact.
analysis_summary.result: No confirmed Patchstack-eligible vulnerability was reproducible in the bundled redux-framework plugin.
analysis_summary.key_observation: Several AJAX handlers use a flawed `!is_user_logged_in() && !is_admin() && !current_user_can(...)` condition, but the packaged plugin only exposes the required user-scoped nonces inside admin-only Redux UI surfaces.
tooling_notes: Phase 1 Semgrep was used as a signal source only.

negative_findings.title: Fixed-name AJAX capability-bypass pattern is nonce-gated and not reproducible for low-privileged users in the shipped plugin

evidence.note: Weak boolean guard before the AJAX notice-dismiss sink.
Dismiss nonce is minted only when the Redux admin notice renders.
Weak boolean guard on `redux_get_icons`.
Request still requires `redux_icon_nonce`.
The icon-select nonce is only rendered in the Redux field UI.
Weak boolean guard on `redux_color_schemes`.
Color-scheme actions still require a valid `redux_{opt_name}_color_schemes` nonce.
High-impact sink candidate: scheme import writes a file via `put_contents`.
Color-scheme nonce is rendered only in the Redux field UI.
Weak boolean guard on `redux_custom_font_timer`.
Weak boolean guard on `redux_custom_fonts`.
High-impact sink candidate: recursive directory deletion.
Custom-font nonce is rendered only in the Redux field UI.
Weak boolean guard on widget-area deletion.
Widget deletion still requires `delete-redux-widget_area-nonce`.
Delete nonce is only rendered on `widgets.php`.
Redux defaults `page_permissions` to `manage_options`.
Redux options pages are registered with `page_permissions`.
The bundled sample config keeps `page_permissions` at `manage_options`.

reasoning.hypothesis: Because the handlers use `&&` instead of `||`, any logged-in user might reach privileged AJAX actions such as scheme import, custom-font deletion, widget-area deletion, or notice dismissal.
reasoning.trace: The source is authenticated AJAX input reaching `update_user_meta`, `put_contents`, recursive `rmdir`, and theme-mod updates in the handlers listed above.
reasoning.defenses: Every traced handler also verifies a WordPress nonce: either a user-and-notice specific token or a field-specific token such as `redux_icon_nonce`, `redux_custom_fonts`, `redux_{opt_name}_color_schemes`, or `delete-redux-widget_area-nonce`.
reasoning.refutation: Those nonces are created only when the matching Redux/admin UI is rendered. In the shipped plugin, the relevant UIs are the Redux options page, `widgets.php`, or the Redux admin notice itself. The bundled config keeps the options page at `manage_options`, and WordPress nonces are user-scoped, so a subscriber cannot reuse an admin's token.
reasoning.conclusion: The boolean guard is poor hardening, but no subscriber or unauthenticated source for a matching valid nonce was found in the packaged plugin.

negative_findings.reopen_conditions: Show a bundled low-privileged page that renders one of these nonces to the same low-privileged user, or a second bug that lets that user mint or steal a valid user-scoped nonce.

negative_findings.title: Dynamic save and export endpoints are also nonce-gated behind admin-only Redux surfaces in the packaged plugin

evidence.note: AJAX save requires `redux_ajax_nonce{opt_name}` before parsing option data.
Weak boolean guard exists, but only after the nonce check.
Sink candidate: validated option write via `options_class->set(...)`.
The AJAX-save nonce is rendered only inside the Redux admin panel.
Export handler uses the same weak boolean pattern.
Export still requires `redux_io_{opt_name}`.
The export nonce is rendered only in the import/export Redux field.
Customizer save registers a dynamic AJAX action.
Customizer save nonce is rendered only inside customizer controls.
Customizer save reuses the weak boolean guard.
Customizer save still requires `redux_customer_nonce`.

reasoning.hypothesis: A low-privileged authenticated user may be able to save or export Redux options through the dynamic AJAX routes.
reasoning.trace: The save route would let the caller mutate the Redux option array; the export route would disclose the current option object; the customizer route would persist merged option data.
reasoning.defenses: All three routes require user-scoped nonces generated inside the Redux panel or the customizer controls.
reasoning.refutation: In the shipped plugin the panel is registered with `manage_options`, and the customizer surface is still an admin/theme capability surface rather than a subscriber surface. No bundled low-privileged UI was found that emits these tokens.
reasoning.conclusion: No practical low-privilege exploit path was demonstrated for the distributed plugin.

negative_findings.reopen_conditions: Show a bundled configuration where a subscriber/customer can legitimately render the panel/customizer nonce, or a nonce disclosure bug reachable by that role.

negative_findings.title: Bundled shortcode XSS signals were refuted

evidence.note: `blog_info()` sanitizes the selector with `sanitize_key()` and escapes the returned value with `esc_html()` or `esc_url()`.
`theme_info()` sanitizes the selector, constrains it to a fixed map, and escapes the output.
`date()` constrains the format string to an allowlist and escapes the rendered output.
`social_profiles` reads values from the Redux option array rather than from shortcode attributes.
The bundled settings page that populates those options is admin-only (`manage_options`).

reasoning.hypothesis: Contributor-usable shortcodes might reflect attacker-controlled attributes or stored option values into HTML without escaping.
reasoning.trace: The Phase 1 anomalies pointed at `blog_info`, `theme_info`, `date`, and the social-profiles shortcode renderer.
reasoning.defenses: The bundled shortcodes now sanitize selectors and escape their return values directly. The social-profiles shortcode pulls URLs/icons/colors from the Redux option array rather than from author-supplied shortcode attributes.
reasoning.refutation: No contributor-controlled attribute reaches an HTML sink in `blog_info`, `theme_info`, or `date`. For `social_profiles`, the stored data source is the admin-only Redux options page, so there is no subscriber/contributor-controlled stored XSS source in the packaged plugin.
reasoning.conclusion: The bundled shortcode candidates are not a reproducible low-privileged XSS issue.

negative_findings.reopen_conditions: Show a bundled path where a contributor or lower role can write the stored social-profile option values, or a shortcode attribute that reaches an unescaped HTML sink.

negative_findings.title: Stored-option XSS signal in the plugin activation notice is not user-controlled

evidence.note: The stored notice value is constructed from translation strings and an internally generated nonce-bearing link.
The notice is echoed without escaping, which triggered the pattern match.

reasoning.hypothesis: A value loaded from `ReduxFrameworkPlugin_ACTIVATED_NOTICES` is echoed without escaping and could be stored XSS.
reasoning.trace: The only stored writer in this plugin path is `single_activate()`, which appends a fixed notice string and a nonce-signed internal link before `admin_notices()` echoes it.
reasoning.defenses: The stored content is framework-controlled, not sourced from request data or a lower-privileged option editor.
reasoning.refutation: No attacker-controlled write to `ReduxFrameworkPlugin_ACTIVATED_NOTICES` was found in the plugin package.
reasoning.conclusion: This is a pattern-match false positive, not an exploitable stored XSS.

negative_findings.reopen_conditions: Show a request-driven or lower-privileged code path that can write arbitrary HTML into `ReduxFrameworkPlugin_ACTIVATED_NOTICES`.

negative_findings.title: User-meta privilege-escalation signal is constrained to registered profile fields and protected profile saves

evidence.note: The save handler is wired to `personal_options_update` and `edit_user_profile_update`.
Saving requires `current_user_can( 'edit_user', $user_id )`.
Saving also requires a dedicated `redux_users_meta_nonce`.
Allowed keys come from `Redux_Users::$fields[opt_name]`, not from arbitrary attacker-chosen meta names.
The sink is `update_user_meta( $user_id, $key, $value, $prev_value )`.

reasoning.hypothesis: A user could supply a privileged meta key such as `wp_capabilities` and escalate their role via `update_user_meta()`.
reasoning.trace: Semgrep matched the user-meta sink in `user_meta_save()`.
reasoning.defenses: The handler only runs on WordPress profile update hooks, requires `edit_user`, requires a nonce, and iterates over keys sourced from the Redux field registry.
reasoning.refutation: No bundled profile configuration exposes an attacker-controlled arbitrary meta-key input; the key space is determined by Redux profile field definitions rather than raw request keys.
reasoning.conclusion: No arbitrary meta-key write or role-escalation path was demonstrated.

negative_findings.reopen_conditions: Show a bundled profile field definition that lets the caller control the meta key itself, or another path that injects `wp_capabilities` into the allowed key set.

out_of_scope.title: Framework-consumer dependent privilege issues remain possible if a downstream product exposes Redux UI nonces to lower roles

evidence.note: Redux defaults `page_permissions` to `manage_options`.
Options pages inherit the configured `page_permissions`.
The shipped sample config does not lower access below admin.

out_of_scope.reasoning: If a downstream plugin or theme deliberately lowers `page_permissions`, exposes the same Redux field UIs on profile/metabox/customizer screens available to weaker roles, or otherwise leaks user-scoped nonces, the weak boolean guards documented above could become exploitable. That scenario was not reproducible in the packaged `redux-framework` plugin, so it is recorded as a framework hardening note rather than an in-scope vulnerability.
